rows.grounds: those to whom one becomes dear

items.question: What attainments make a practitioner dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment are named together.
The yoginīs are the ones to whom one becomes dear.
Becoming dear is expressed as a potential outcome.
items.inference: A practitioner possessing enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment may become dear to the yoginīs.
items.plain_english: One may become dear to the yoginīs, attaining enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the section emerging in Candra-dvīpa?
premises: A section is described as having emerged in Candra-dvīpa.
A chapter is identified by an ordinal number.
The chapter is named as the ninth.
items.inference: The ninth chapter concludes in the section emerging in Candra-dvīpa.
items.plain_english: This is the ninth chapter, in the section that emerged in Candra-dvīpa.

items.question: In what posture and condition is the self to be visualized?
premises: The self is described as surrounded by fire.
The self is described as standing.
The standing is supported on one foot.
items.inference: The self is to be visualized standing on one foot and surrounded by fire.
items.plain_english: Visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What has been made manifest to the speaker by the god today?
premises: The speaker addresses the god directly.
The determination of knowledge is the object revealed.
The revelation is said to have occurred today.
items.inference: The determination of knowledge has been made manifest to the speaker today by the god.
items.plain_english: O God, today the determination of knowledge has been made manifest to me.

items.question: What division is sought to be known fully and without limit?
premises: A division of eight octads is named.
The purpose is to know this division fully.
The knowing is described as endless.
items.inference: The division of eight octads is sought to be known fully and endlessly.
uncertainties: The exact sense of anantathā in this context is somewhat ambiguous.
items.plain_english: And to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.

items.question: How is the wheel accomplished in the secret place according to Bhairava?
premises: A secret place is named as the locus.
The wheel is the subject of accomplishment.
The accomplishment occurs quickly.
items.inference: In the secret place, O Bhairava, the wheel is quickly accomplished.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, explain how the wheel is quickly accomplished in the secret place.

rows.grounds: those for whom it is hard to obtain

items.question: How does Bhairava respond to the great goddess's difficult question?
premises: Bhairava expresses approval twice.
Bhairava states he has been asked.
The matter asked about is hard for gods to obtain.
items.inference: Bhairava approves the question and acknowledges being asked about something rare even for the gods.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess! I have been asked about something hard to obtain even for the gods.

items.question: Where are the syllables kṣa and laṃ located in the subtle body?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra.
The syllable laṃ is named next.
The syllable laṃ is located in the forehead.
items.inference: The syllable kṣa is at the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region.
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is at the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Where are the syllables ṣa and śa located in the subtle body?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region.
The syllable śa is named next.
The syllable śa is placed in the heart.
items.inference: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region and the syllable śa is in the heart.
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.

items.question: What is the listener invited to hear after the place-wheels are declared?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared.
A meditation pertaining to them is mentioned.
The beloved is commanded to hear it.
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the speaker invites the beloved to hear their meditation.
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first octad described for meditation?
premises: A divine lotus is the object described.
The lotus has eight spokes.
The lotus is adorned by the first octad.
items.inference: The meditation object is a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.
items.plain_english: Visualize a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner with an equal mind abandon through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an equal mind.
Village customs are named as something to relinquish.
The abandonment is expressed as an injunction.
items.inference: Through practice, one with an equal mind should abandon village customs.
uncertainties: grāma-dharmañ may refer broadly to conventional social duties.
items.plain_english: Through practice, becoming even-minded, one should abandon the customs of ordinary village life.

items.question: What powers arise from this practice according to the teaching given to the beloved?
premises: Knowledge of distant hearing is named.
Paralysis of bonds is named.
Both are presented together as outcomes.
items.inference: The practice yields knowledge of distant hearing and the paralysis of bonds.
uncertainties: pāśa-stobham could also imply arresting or stunning of fetters.
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of distant hearing and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further attainments are briefly stated for the goddess?
premises: Immortality is named as an attainment.
Transformation is named as another attainment.
The statement is given in brief.
items.inference: In brief, the attainments include immortality and transformation.
uncertainties: The specific nature of parivartanam is not fully specified.
items.plain_english: O goddess, in brief, there is also immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled lotus characterized in meditation?
premises: A second lotus is introduced.
The lotus has eight petals.
It is well illuminated by meditation on fire.
items.inference: The second eight-petaled lotus is well illuminated through meditation on fire.
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled lotus, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation.
The practitioner makes forms.
The forms are made in many ways.
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.

items.question: What destructive power is attributed to the practitioner when angered?
premises: The practitioner is described as angry.
The action is the destruction of all.
The triple world with moving and unmoving beings is the object.
items.inference: When angry, the practitioner may destroy the entire triple world with all moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all its moving and unmoving beings.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: A third great wheel is introduced.
Nine principles are named in relation to it.
The wheel is described as a liberator.
items.inference: The third great wheel functions as the liberator from the nine principles.
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual benefits result from this wheel's practice?
premises: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair is named.
Seeing from very far away is named.
Both are presented as resulting benefits.
items.inference: The practice brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair and the power of seeing from very far away.
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

items.question: What practice should be performed in solitude with focused intent?
premises: The practice is to be done in solitude.
One should make many forms and perform meditation.
The practitioner must be intent on that practice.
items.inference: In solitude, intent on the practice, one should perform meditation and assume many forms.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on the practice, make many forms and perform meditation.

items.question: What result comes to one intent on constant practice?
premises: The practitioner is intent on constant practice.
The action produces a specific result.
The result named is immortality.
items.inference: One intent on constant practice attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one intent on constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: What outcome is promised through abstaining from food by day?
premises: Non-eating by day is specified as the means.
Death associated with age is named as the object.
A future overcoming of that death is stated.
items.inference: By abstaining from food by day, one will overcome death due to age.
uncertainties: The exact sense of gamiṣyate with mṛtyuṃ is interpretive; it suggests passing beyond or overcoming death.
items.plain_english: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death due to aging.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant practice of this yoga?
premises: The means is yoga of constant practice.
A specific age-form is indicated as two times eight years.
The practitioner becomes that form.
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power arises from always contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: A smoke-colored form is to be contemplated always.
The triple world is named as the object affected.
The practitioner may shake that world.
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world.
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
